# Azure FinOps Agent — Copilot Instructions

## Purpose

Azure FinOps Agent is an open-source Azure sample and delivery accelerator. It combines conversational AI with Azure Cost Management, ARM, Resource Graph, Advisor, Microsoft Graph, Log Analytics, public pricing, file analysis, visualizations, remediation scripts, and scheduled jobs.

It is designed for customers to deploy into **their own tenant and subscription**. Never commit maintainer or customer tenant IDs, subscription IDs, resource IDs, generated resource names, app IDs, user principal names, email addresses, IP addresses, connection strings, or deployment credentials.

## Stack

- Backend: .NET 10 minimal API in `src/Dashboard`
- Frontend: Vue 3 + Vite + ECharts in `src/Dashboard/frontend`
- Agent runtime: Microsoft Agent Framework (`Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry`): one `AIProjectClient.AsAIAgent(ChatClientAgentOptions)` agent over the Foundry project Responses API. `AzureOpenAI:Endpoint` is the project endpoint (or the account endpoint plus `AzureOpenAI:ProjectName`).
- Default model: `gpt-6.1-sol`, version `2026-09-29`, using the Responses API at reasoning effort `medium` (`AzureOpenAI:ReasoningEffort`; CI deploys the gate-tested `EVAL_REASONING_EFFORT`). Turns are dominated by model time: on gpt-6.1-sol a round at `xhigh` takes about 45 s against about 15 s at `medium`. Live evaluations use the same model for the agent and the judge (`EVAL_MODEL`/`EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL` in the `ai-evaluation` GitHub environment decide what CI deploys). Existing-account reuse requires that deployment and a Foundry project to exist and the app identity to have account-scoped **Foundry User** (formerly Azure AI User); **Cognitive Services OpenAI User** does not cover the project Responses endpoint, and the evaluation identity needs the same role. Verify available model-specific quota; deleting a different model does not free its quota. gpt-6.1-sol does not support the Priority service tier.
- Authentication: anonymous chat plus optional multi-tenant Entra OAuth
- Hosting: Linux container on Azure App Service
- Infrastructure: `azure.yaml` + Bicep under `infra`
- Observability: OpenTelemetry + Application Insights

`Microsoft.Agents.AI.*`, `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.*`, `Azure.AI.Projects` and `ModelContextProtocol.*` are one compatibility unit; bump them together (Dependabot groups them) and prefer built-in Agent Framework, SDK and Microsoft services over host code: before building a component, check whether Microsoft already provides it (for example the SDK's own HTTP 429 retry, or Microsoft Learn's MCP server for documentation). Do not add a host-built agent loop, a second model client or a per-scenario agent.

## Core architecture

- One singleton `AIAgent` serves every conversation. Each turn passes the owner's plain `AIFunction` tools through `ChatClientAgentRunOptions`; `AllowConcurrentInvocation` runs independent calls in parallel. The owner binding lives in the tool instances (each built from that user's tokens), not in a wrapper.
- Each `AgentConversation` stores `session.json` (the serialized `AgentSession`, i.e. the chained previous-response ID, plus listing metadata) and the host-owned UI transcript `events.jsonl` under the owner's directory in `AGENT_HOME` (default `/home/copilot`, kept for existing data; the legacy `COPILOT_HOME` variable is read as a fallback); Entra users are isolated by the validated `tid + oid` pair and anonymous users by generated user ID. Never treat OID alone as globally unique. An OID-only legacy workdir is admissible only when its encrypted identity record attests the same pair.
- One `SemaphoreSlim` gate per user serializes conversation create/open/delete. Do not bypass it: warmup and transcript replay otherwise race on the live-session registry.
- One active turn per session is enforced by `ChatEndpoints`; scheduled jobs use the same turn gate.
- SSE streams deltas, reasoning, timing, tools, charts, generated files, scores, cooldowns, busy/errors, and completion.
- The backend continues a turn after browser disconnect and persists the answer. The frontend reconciles against the server turn gate and transcript.
- OAuth access tokens stay in memory. Only the encrypted refresh-token identity record is persisted.
- The project client uses a `TokenCredential` (system-assigned managed identity in Azure; Azure CLI or environment credentials locally). Never bake a static model token into a conversation.
- The model sees only host-registered tools plus the model's hosted web search tool (`AzureOpenAI:WebSearch`, default on at the maintainer's request; Bicep `aoaiWebSearch`/`AZURE_OPENAI_WEB_SEARCH`, evaluator `EVAL_WEB_SEARCH`). Its queries go to Bing grounding, outside the Azure data boundary, so the prompt limits it to recent public information no API returns, and every model request caps hosted calls with the Responses API `max_tool_calls` (`AgentSessionFactory.WebSearchCallsPerResponse` = 1; the service stops at about one more, and function calls are not counted); the guidance takes precedence over the platform's general browsing instruction by treating `QueryAzure` and the Learn tools as the live web request tools whose results already satisfy it; tenant data, list prices (including Azure OpenAI/Foundry token prices) and API contracts still come from `QueryAzure`, and Microsoft documentation from Microsoft Learn's MCP server. That server (`https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp`, `MicrosoftLearn:Enabled`, default on) is connected with the official MCP C# SDK (`MicrosoftLearnMcp`); its `microsoft_docs_search` and `microsoft_docs_fetch` tools are passed to the agent unchanged as Agent Framework MCP tools, not as the hosted Responses MCP tool, whose calls would share the `max_tool_calls` web-search cap. The host only keeps one connection, replaces it after a transport failure and retries that call once (calls that failed together share the replacement; a JSON-RPC protocol error goes back to the model unchanged), passes a structured result's text once instead of also its `structuredContent` copy (an error keeps its JSON and `isError` flag), and cuts a result above 48 KB with a note. `WebSearchGuard` (the model client under Agent Framework's function loop, set through `AsAIAgent`'s `clientFactory`, with per-turn state on `ToolExecutionContext`) lets a turn start a hosted web search only in its first model response: later requests offer it only to continue a search already started (open a page it found), and never after a Learn tool call. Prompt rules alone did not stop the model from re-checking evidence an API had just returned (`site:learn.microsoft.com` searches, opening the Retail Prices URL it had queried); the prompt tells the model to make any needed search in its first response. Search terms go to a public service, so the prompt keeps tenant, resource and user names out of them. There is no shell, file system, code execution or other MCP server.
- Tools run through Agent Framework's own `FunctionInvokingChatClient` without a host wrapper. Its `FunctionInvoker` only normalizes known model argument quirks (`ModelJson.Normalize`: a `recipient_name`/`parameters` envelope naming the invoked tool, and numbers/booleans/JSON for string-only parameters) and records each call's execution time in the ambient `ToolExecutionContext`; `IncludeDetailedErrors` returns exception messages to the model. `AgentConversation` publishes tool start/complete events from the streamed `FunctionCallContent`/`FunctionResultContent`; parallel results arrive together after the whole batch, so `tool_done.durationMs` is the measured execution time rather than the wait since the model wrote the call. `TurnExecution` records evidence from what each tool returned. Stop cancels the run's token; the turn gate is held until the run reports a terminal state.
- The response chain advances only after a successful run, so a stopped or failed turn leaves the previous response ID and never leaves unanswered tool calls. A stream whose last model response ends without a finish reason or usage, or that reports an error, is a failed run (`ModelRunCompletion`), never an empty answer. The SDK already retries HTTP 408/429/5xx with backoff; a model rate limit that still fails the run is shown as a plain busy notice (`ModelRunCompletion.BusyMessage`), never the provider text naming the deployment, region and quota. An expired chain (`previous response` 400/404) resets to a fresh model context. The service retains stored responses (about 30 days); deleting a conversation deletes local state only.
- Long chains are slow: production calls above about 180k input tokens waited 10-17 s for a first token. When a completed turn's largest model input exceeds `AgentConversation.CompactAfterInputTokens` (100k), the next turn starts a fresh model context carrying a bounded recap of the visible questions and answers (no tool results, no injected context), the files earlier turns generated or the user attached (images are no longer visible, so the recap says to ask for them again) and the code of the latest generated script. A pending approval postpones it. Any turn starting a fresh context (`StartsFreshContext`) must receive the per-session connection/upload context again, because `ChatEndpoints` otherwise sends it once per session.
- The reasoning summary streams as unpersisted `reasoning` deltas, with a paragraph break between summary parts, and each segment persists as a `thinking` event (`ReasoningEvent`) that the restored transcript returns as the message's `thinking`. Session audits exclude it as private model reasoning.
- Nothing about tool responses is stored. `QueryAzure` returns a response up to 32 KB whole; a larger one returns its HTTP/timestamp preamble, a `Coverage:` line with the root coverage fields (`complete`, `pagesRead`, `_finops`, `nextLink`…) and the schema inferred by `JsonQuery` (property names, CLR types, counts, samples and a starter expression), so the model repeats the request with `query`, a Dynamic LINQ (System.Linq.Dynamic.Core) C# expression over the response root `it`. Only the query's JSON result (≤48 KB, truncated lists noted) returns, after the `Coverage:` line. Column/row tables become row objects, other text becomes `it.lines`. `query` without `url` is a calculator that sends no request and is not source evidence. The query sandbox: case-sensitive members, no `new` beyond anonymous objects and value types, only LINQ/string/Math/Convert/DateTime/TimeSpan/Guid members (no `GetType`, reflection, `PadLeft`, `Format`, `Join`, dynamic `Replace` or large `ToString` formats; no list `IndexOf`/`FindIndex` or `(x, i) =>` lambdas, whose errors name `lines.TakeWhile(...).Count()`/`SkipWhile(...).Take(n)` instead), a 4,000-character expression, a 20M-step/10-second budget with cancellation, 64K-character strings and the output cap; a call inside a lambda that reads only the root (a per-item share's `root.value.Sum(...)`) is evaluated once. Reads are JSON-forgiving: members absent from the response (named in the result), null navigation, missing keys/indexes and empty lists read as null/empty; keyed objects used as collections or read by string key (`parameters["effect"]`) become dictionaries; booleans are `bool?`, so predicates compare them (`== true`) and a bare one fails naming that fix, while string tests (`Contains`) already return `bool` and are negated with `!` alone; a negated method-call or parenthesized test compared with `false` (or `!= true`) cancels its own `!`, so `JsonQuery.CancelledNegation` rejects it before any request (`HTTP 400 … No request was sent.`) and `Evaluate` rejects it for calculations; never-seen members used numerically are `double?`, and ones the query iterates are lists; a never-seen node gains only the members the query reads through it; a case-only member mismatch stays an error. A query error returns the error plus the schema. Keep approval/chart/score/artifact control messages inline; never expose host paths.
- Gates, cooldowns, and registries are process-local. Run one active app instance; shared files are persistence, not distributed coordination.

## Security invariants

The agent can read and apply approved non-destructive changes, but it never deletes Azure resources.

- `DELETE` is blocked centrally for Azure and Graph pass-through tools.
- Azure `POST` is restricted to the read-only allowlist in `AzureQueryTools`; action endpoints such as start, restart, deallocate, power-off, and reservation return are blocked.
- ARM `PUT` and `PATCH` run only through `ApplyAzureChange`, an `ApprovalRequiredAIFunction`. Agent Framework holds the call and the UI shows its exact method, URL and body; the next chat turn carries the user's `approval: {requestId, approved}` and only that explicit approval runs it under the user's RBAC. Any other message rejects every held change, an approval that no longer matches a held request is refused as `approval_stale` before dispatch, and a prompt cannot approve a write. `QueryAzure` refuses `PUT`/`PATCH` with 405.
- Destructive recommendations must use `GenerateScript` so the user reviews and runs them.
- Every session, job, upload, generated artifact, and transcript endpoint must enforce per-user ownership.
- Standard add-on consent tiers are read-only. Graph writes require separately granted write scopes.
- Never log or return bearer tokens, refresh tokens, secrets, authorization headers, or connection strings.
- The host does not screen or redact chat, job, tool or SSE content for credentials; recognizing and refusing secrets is left to the model (maintainer decision). Model prompt/response content capture is off. Users must not paste credentials.

### Untrusted-input rules

Treat every model-authored tool argument as attacker-controlled: it is shaped by uploaded file contents, fetched pages, Azure resource names, and tags.

- A file path, blob name, URL, or command fragment must never come from a tool argument. The host resolves it from a per-user registry keyed by an opaque id.
- When a free-form JSON parameter bag is merged into a host-built request, reject host-owned keys explicitly. Merging the model's object last silently lets it override them.
- Filesystem readers take a base directory from the host, resolve the candidate with `realpath`, and require containment. Fail closed when the root is absent; an existence check is not a containment check.
- Error paths must not echo the requested path or resource id back to the model — that is a probing oracle.
- Anything reaching `v-html` is entity-escaped first, at the single entry point. Escaping only some subfragments (table cells, attributes) is not enough.
- Model-supplied chart/render options are allow-listed and stripped of DOM and HTML sinks before they reach a renderer.

## Authentication

OAuth tiers are resource-specific and delegated:

| Tier           | Resource               | Scopes                                                   |
| -------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `base`         | Azure Resource Manager | `user_impersonation`                                     |
| `licenses`     | Microsoft Graph        | `User.Read`, `Organization.Read.All`, `Reports.Read.All` |
| `chargeback`   | Microsoft Graph        | `User.Read`, `User.Read.All`, `Group.Read.All`           |
| `loganalytics` | Log Analytics          | `Data.Read`                                              |
| `storage`      | Azure Storage          | `user_impersonation`                                     |

`tier=all` walks only the remaining add-on tiers through separate user-scoped consent screens. Do not combine cross-resource scopes or replace this with tenant-wide admin consent.

Disconnect/revoke/logout differ intentionally:

- Disconnect clears live/session tokens and the browser identity cookie, but retains the encrypted identity record for explicit reconnect.
- Revoke clears the cookie and encrypted identity record and forces fresh consent next time.
- Logout clears Entra identity and immediately assigns a new anonymous chat identity.

Before manually testing a fresh consent flow, revoke existing grants for the test app in the selected test tenant. Use placeholders or local configuration—never commit real values.

## Tool patterns

The agent is deliberately minimal: tools are thin, host-enforced pass-throughs and the model authors every API call. Do not reintroduce host-built composite tools, host-computed headlines/tables/summaries, or per-scenario KQL/REST builders to fix an evaluation; improve the prompt or tool description instead so the model investigates and calls the right API itself.

- Evidence tools: `QueryAzure` for every HTTP evidence source (ARM, Microsoft Graph, Log Analytics/Application Insights, Blob Storage exports, Azure Retail Prices, official documentation/specs and public pages), plus `QueryUploadedFile`. `ApplyAzureChange` is the only write path. Host code owns only exact-host credential routing, security, scope, throttling, pagination and cropping rules.
- Descriptions tell the model to look up rather than guess: `GET /providers/{namespace}` for a provider's resource types (which name its operations), the official OpenAPI specs in [Azure/azure-rest-api-specs](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs) (browse through the api.github.com contents API, read through raw.githubusercontent.com and crop the spec JSON with `query`), [microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata](https://github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata) and Microsoft Learn through its MCP tools (`microsoft_docs_search`, then `microsoft_docs_fetch` only when the passages are not enough; when those tools are unavailable, Learn's own search API through `QueryAzure`). A failed call fails the evaluation, so verification comes before the call.
- ARM api-versions come from ARM itself, never from the prompt or tool descriptions (`ModelFacingTextNamesNoDatedApiVersion` guards this). A read without `api-version` is first sent with the placeholder `9999-12-31`: ARM rejects it by naming the resource type's supported versions, and the host sends the newest stable one, noted in root `_apiVersion` and kept per resource type for an hour (a later rejection replaces it). A provider that checks no version answers the placeholder itself, which providers treat as their newest. No manifest, version or product list is stored. Writes keep an explicit api-version so the approved URL is the URL sent. Explicit model versions are honored.
- Evidence semantics: a failed, denied or unqueried read is unknown, never zero, but a successful read is evidence: an optional property it omits is not set (its documented default, never "unconfirmed"), and a 404 whose error code names the missing item (`AzureQueryTools.IsAbsent`: a specific `…NotFound` code, never a bare `NotFound`, which a wrong path also returns; batched reads count them in their banner) shows it is absent. Access failures name the missing Azure role or the consent button to use; admin APIs with no access tier (Intune, Defender, Entra role management) get a script the admin runs, never an instruction to change this app's registration. The user's stated goal and constraints come first: replicating a setup uses its exact values with a better practice as one note, valid alternatives are named rather than one path presented as required, and names, regions and values come from the user or a read, never from an example.
- The system prompt keeps a short list of API facts that prevent common failed calls (Cost Management grouping limits, Resource Graph scope/KQL rules, tenant-scope reservation listing, which needs tenant-level benefit reader roles and is called only for commitment questions, and the subscription offers Cost Management does not support, recognized by the `quotaId` carried in the discovered-scope context). Keep it short and factual; do not grow it into per-question recipes.
- `GenerateScript` is always loaded. When the user requests Azure CLI or PowerShell code, or a Bicep or ARM template, call it directly with the complete code in `scriptContent` (`language` `bash`, `powershell`, `bicep` or `arm`; an ARM template must be one JSON object with `$schema`, `contentVersion` and `resources`). A requested template is the template itself, never a script that writes it. The tool packages an owner-bound artifact and never executes or deploys the code. Script delivery is a proposed savings action, never an executed change. See [the tool and prompt catalog](../docs/tool-catalog.md) for registration flags, inputs and limits; update it when these contracts change.
- Tools return raw API JSON. `QueryAzure` converts successful CSV/XML to queryable JSON and crops it statelessly with the model's `query`, so the model filters, projects, groups, counts and calculates inside one expression (several views as one anonymous object). Totals, counts, shares, rankings, comparisons, token-cost estimates and running totals come from `query` (`Sum`, `Math.Round`, `GroupBy`, a `root.…Where(r => r.date <= d).Sum(…)` running total), never mental arithmetic; round money with `Math.Round(x, 2)`. Follow-up GETs over a returned list are the url lines of one `QueryAzure` call built from query results; the prompt, not host code, tells the model to copy each item exactly.
- Prefer string parameters for scalars; SDK coercion of numeric arguments can be unreliable. `ModelJson.Normalize` (run by the function invoker) converts JSON numbers/booleans supplied for string-only parameters to strings before binding. Parameters that carry JSON use `JsonElement? name = null`, which emits an untyped optional schema so the model passes native JSON instead of escaping it in a string (a `JsonElement` default of `default` breaks schema generation). A nullable C# parameter is not optional in the emitted schema: give optional inputs real defaults and test requiredness plus omitted-argument invocation.
- Query arithmetic establishes calculations, not price validity or deployability. Surface tool `Error:` results as failures even when the function call itself succeeded.
- `PublishFAQ` must be explicitly requested. Preserve host authentication/moderation checks and never describe pending review as publication.
- Public web reads go through `QueryAzure` public GET routing. The SSRF guard blocks literal private, loopback, link-local and metadata hosts before DNS, connects only to public IPs after DNS and redirects, disables proxy/cookies/auth, honors the host cancellation token and one deadline through body reading, and reports transport failure explicitly.
- Reuse one HTTP client/session where applicable; do not create clients per request. Tools generally do not catch API exceptions internally.
- Resource Graph POST bodies require one explicit nonempty `subscriptions` or `managementGroups` array. Cost Management, Consumption and PolicyInsights paths require a scope prefix; tenant-root `reservationSummaries` is rejected in favour of discovered reservation-order or billing scopes.
- ARM transport repairs stay narrow and visible: a read whose api-version ARM rejects while listing supported versions is retried once with the newest listed stable version; an unlisted `UnsupportedApiVersion` asks ARM for the type's versions with the placeholder and tries at most two older stable ones; both annotate root `_apiVersion`. `body` and `scores` are `JsonElement?` parameters, so the model passes native JSON; `ModelJson` only reads a JSON string leniently (trailing commas, comments) and never repairs garbled JSON. A subscription-prefixed Resource Graph path is routed to the provider path only when the body already lists that subscription. `HttpHelper` retries dropped connections for GET only, never for POST/PUT/PATCH. A Cost Management query's `Dimension` grouping named `Currency` (which the service rejects and which every row already carries as a column) is removed and reported in root `_request`; a `TagKey` named Currency is kept. Never widen these into guessing paths, scopes, bodies or values.
- Parallelize independent calls except Cost Management `/query` and `/forecast`, which are tenant-throttled. Same-kind GETs (one per region, subscription or scope) are several `url` lines of one `QueryAzure` call: at most 50 GET-only lines without body, run at most 4 at a time, each cropped by the same `query` as its own response, a schema shared by several large responses shown once, and any failed line reported as `PARTIAL RESULT` (unknown, not empty). Other independent reads are parallel calls in one response; the host serializes cost query/forecast calls per tenant, retries once after a service delay of at most five minutes, keeps `retryAtUtc`/`willRetry` in cooldown SSE events, and stops after a final 429 for the rest of the turn. Cost Management permits at most two grouping dimensions; the host rejects more before dispatch.
- Preserve `_finops`/`sourceEvidence`, retry deadlines and partial coverage. The cost cache is credential/request-bound; never label cached or unknown-age billing data as freshly measured.
- `QueryUploadedFile` uses `jsonPath` for JSON selectors and supports 1-50 output columns after filtering/aggregation/sorting; host `path`, `kind` and `mode` remain reserved. XLSX `workbook` returns all sheets' shapes and numeric summaries in one call.
- `GetSavingsLedger` supports status/category/literal scopeContains filters and string limit/offset paging (default 50, maximum 200, limit=0 for totals); totals cover all matches before paging.

### Retail pricing

- Retail prices are `QueryAzure` GETs to `https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices?currencyCode=USD&$filter=<OData>`. The host pins the origin, requires `$filter`, drops `$top`/`$skip`, defaults api-version and USD, follows only same-origin `NextPageLink` under the fixed 10-page host cap, retries 429/5xx and returns raw `Items` with `retrievedAtUtc`, `pages` and `complete`.
- Compare several regions or SKUs with `or` in one filter and use `query` to select compatible rows; a multi-service estimate fetches every component in the first round as parallel calls. Some services, such as Load Balancer, publish only an `armRegionName 'Global'` rate; Azure SQL vCore compute rows exclude the per-vCore `SQL License` meter, which is also Global-only and must be added for license-included pricing. Meter, product and SKU names are not derivable from ARM SKUs; the model starts from structural fields and reads returned values instead of guessing. The QueryAzure Retail Prices entry is the complete contract (no documentation lookup or web search first), and unit conversions (per-1M from token meters published per `1K` on older families and per `1M` on newer GPT generations, monthly from hourly) happen in the same `query` that selects the rows, never in a web search. Foundry model families are separate `productName`s under `serviceName 'Foundry Models'`; the system prompt describes them, the newer meter abbreviations (Std Gl, Std DZ, PP, Cd Inp, Cd Wr, ShortCo/LongCo) and the PTU hourly and reservation rows, so "latest models" questions query every family instead of only `Azure OpenAI`. Prompts, the system prompt and tool descriptions name model brands and families only, never a model version (maintainer decision): a hardcoded version ages and steers the agent away from the newest models in the price list or a web search. Test fixtures may use real meter names as API data. Meter spellings change case between releases (`glbl`/`Glbl`) and both the Retail Prices `contains` and the query sandbox are case-sensitive, so the guidance matches with `tolower`/`ToLower()`. A family's newest model is the highest version in its meter or SKU names; `effectiveStartDate` is when a price took effect, not a release date (an older model re-priced later carries a later date), so it only selects a meter's current price. The Retail Prices next-page link carries an explicit `:443`, so the host compares it as a URI; a link it does not follow reports partial coverage, never `complete`. Benchmark and speed questions are answered directly: one web search for the latest published results while `QueryAzure` fetches prices in parallel, each figure with its source, date and whether it is vendor-reported.
- The prompt keeps pricing quality rules: clarify material configuration (OS/license, tier, fixed-region region) unless the user gave enough context or authorized assumptions, default to on-demand list prices when region and size are given, compare only within one product/meter and volume band, carry qualifiers into labels, and quote the retrieval time, which is not a price-effective date.

### Maturity scoring

- Crawl, Walk, Run and Playbook all use `ReportMaturityScore`. The model gathers the evidence for every dimension defined in that tool's description and submits all of them once. Each dimension `detail` is at most 20 words of decisive figures, and the answer is about 150 words plus one table of at most five rows: the score card already shows every dimension, and output tokens dominate a level's latency (about 8,000 per Crawl at 50-100 tokens/s).
- Unknown and not-applicable scores are null, never zero, and are excluded from the displayed denominator. An empty resource group is not billable waste. Do not claim effective policy enforcement from assignment-name matches. Advisor alternatives overlap and are not additive.

### Compute and operations

- Spot/GPU questions are answered with QueryAzure: Compute usages for quota, Compute SKUs for regional and zone restrictions, the read-only Spot `placementScores/spot/generate` POST, and Resource Graph `SpotResources` for historical eviction rates. Quota, placement scores and prices are not capacity guarantees; missing history is unknown, not zero risk.
- Availability, quota, configuration and allocation are separate claims for every provider; the prompt states this once, product-agnostically, instead of per-product recipes. Availability is read from the provider's own operations and needs no existing resource; quota is valid only at the scope (subscription and region, or one named resource) and compute mode (serverless or dedicated) it was read at and never transfers, including to a resource not yet created; allocation is unverified without a documented signal. A 403, unregistered provider or unsupported operation is unknown, and a missing resource makes its quota not applicable, never zero. Configuration reads project only needed fields, never environment variables, app settings or secrets.
- Treat ordinary Spot eviction and resilience questions as infrastructure questions. Provider content-filter errors are separate from tool failures; inspect structured filter metadata, including `error.content_filters.content_filter_results`, without logging prompts or credentials. Do not silently rewrite user text or automatically retry around moderation. Do not change filter settings autonomously merely to make a test pass.
- **Scoped maintainer exception - filters only:** An explicit maintainer request authorizes supported Azure filter and content-filter configuration changes, including custom RAI policies, configurable severity thresholds, and Bicep policy configuration. Confirm the target deployment and exact policy differences, preserve platform-required protections, avoid unintended changes to shared policies, and verify the effective configuration. Deployment still requires explicit instruction. This allowance does not extend to authentication, authorization/RBAC, ownership checks, write approvals, secret protection, destructive-operation restrictions, or any other security control.
- Network Watcher `connectivityCheck` is an allowlisted `QueryAzure` ARM POST only when the body validates a probe from an existing VM resource ID to one destination address or resourceId and a TCP port from 1-65535. Never substitute connectivity from the app host or broaden it into a scan.
- Nothing records operations host-side. A `201`/`202` from `ApplyAzureChange` is accepted, not complete: the model polls its `Azure-AsyncOperation` or `Location` URL (kept in the result preamble) with `QueryAzure` GET after `Retry-After`. HTTP 202 is not success and unknown writes must not be retried blindly.

### Charts and generated files

- One response contains one chart or one table, not both.
- Answers are written for Azure newcomers (maintainer decision): plain words with each Azure term explained in a few words, a one or two sentence headline, about 50-100 words outside the visual, and at most three one-sentence notes. Tables keep at most six rows and four columns unless the question or a system-prompt rule asks for more, one value or short phrase per cell (no `2 / 4` pairs, never two sentences) and readable numbers and times (2.8 billion tokens, not 2,762.5M; 5 Oct 2026, 21:19 UTC). Detail left out is offered as a follow-up link. Brevity never drops a requested metric or a required qualifier. General guidance questions without tenant data take at most two rounds of Learn reads (searches together, then the one to three best pages only when the returned passages do not answer it); documentation answers carry no retrieval time, while cost, budget, inventory, tag and pricing answers keep theirs.
- Generated script/deck markers are converted into structured SSE events.
- Download endpoints require an authenticated session and owner match.
- Expired artifacts render an expired state rather than a dead link.
- Owner-bound artifacts persist for 24 hours. `GenerateDataReport` creates real CSV/XLSX/escaped HTML with row-count checks and spreadsheet formula neutralization, and a rejected payload names the sheet, row or limit to fix (never cell values); never invent sandbox links.
- Upload ids bind to one conversation. Pending uploads expire in 30 minutes; bound uploads have a 24-hour sliding lease, capped at seven days. Active readers hold leases. Starting another conversation must not delist the previous conversation's files.

## Scheduled jobs

- Jobs are Entra-only and use delegated refresh tokens.
- Every run must report `ReportJobOutcome`. Success requires host-observed complete fresh evidence for every cited request scope, plus a nonempty answer. Turn idle alone is not business success; store the validated outcome, not the model's claim.
- Each run starts with the same `[CONTEXT: …]` block as chat (connected APIs, the subscriptions with their offer `quotaId` and management groups discovered with the run's own token, today's date), sent once per model context. Without it a daily digest on a subscription offer Cost Management does not support reported a "possible delay" every run.
- Compact model context after every 20 completed runs while preserving the durable transcript. Pause on unverifiable compaction, a verified `goal_achieved`, or `action_required` (a blocker waiting cannot clear, such as an unsupported offer or a missing role; the UI shows "needs your action"). Scheduled ARM changes still require explicit UI approval; no unattended capacity purchase.
- Ownership is an exact tenant-ID, object-ID, and pair-derived user-ID match. Legacy jobs without a tenant binding stay disabled; never fall back to OID-only or user-ID-only ownership.
- Limits: 3 active jobs per user; custom cadence 1–43200 minutes; sub-daily expiry 7 days; daily or slower expiry 90 days; 5 consecutive failures auto-pause.
- Resume is cap-checked exactly like create.
- Every job owns one dedicated run-log session; it is hidden from Conversations while the job exists and reappears when the job is deleted.
- Run logs have no composer. They expose Build deck, Summarize runs, and Edit job.
- Create+run-now, explicit run-now, and edit+run-now all call `watchJobRunAndOpen`.
- Templates: capacity check, reserve when available, 1-minute test, daily digest, anomaly watch, budget guard, idle sweep, Advisor watch, and retry last question.

## Frontend invariants

- At 900px and below, the left navigation is an overlay and the right rail is hidden, so on phones everything lives in the left navigation: New chat, Scheduled jobs (signed in only, directly below New chat; the empty state is just the heading and New job), the prompt library (signed out: "AI governance & security" then "AI & LLM pricing" expanded, "Infrastructure pricing" collapsed, each with three or four questions, most important first; each button shows a short customer question of at most 36 characters and sends a precise, slightly technical prompt that names no single model service or version; signed in, all collapsed), and Chats (shown once there is a conversation). Above 900px, Scheduled jobs and Chats render in the right rail instead (one template, moved by a deferred `Teleport` that is disabled on compact screens), so they are never in both places. Menu headings carry no second line (counts appear only for scheduled jobs that exist), and the tenant box is labelled "Tenant ID (optional)" without a separate hint. The right rail shows Scheduled jobs and Chats first, then, only while the conversation has tool calls, its Agent execution; it groups calls under the question that made them, newest first, each headed by its call count, failures and kinds of calls, with only the newest group open (opening an older one scrolls the chat to its question). New chat lives only in the navigation; the top bar has none.
- Conversation deletion is one click with no confirmation step. The row stays visible and disabled while the server responds. Only confirmed server deletion clears client state; active turns return a conflict and failures remain visible for retry. The composer's Clear chat (shown once a conversation has a question and a response, disabled while a turn runs) uses the same deletion and then opens a new chat; a refused deletion keeps the conversation and shows the reason.
- Closed navigation must be invisible and inert. Keep the compact overlay aligned to the actual header, dismissible with Escape/backdrop, and return focus to its toggle.
- Auto-scroll follows only while near the bottom. User scroll-up must never be overridden.
- Hidden browser tabs suspend ResizeObserver, animation frames, transitions, and smooth scrolling. Keep reactive watcher fallbacks.
- Cooldown and activity-indicator motion must respect reduced motion and pause when hidden. Completed replies stay static; wait progress is never task-completion progress, and live countdown or activity-status changes must not repeatedly interrupt screen readers.
- Do not rewrite punctuation in streamed model text. Identifiers such as hostnames, versions, and Azure resource names must remain byte-for-byte intact. The only removal is the model's private-use web-search citation markers (U+E200 `cite` … U+E201), stripped from the final message and by the Markdown renderer.
- A complete assistant `message` event replaces partial streamed deltas and cancels queued text animation. Having received one delta is not a reason to discard the authoritative final message. Cost cooldown notices remain visible in the chat on mobile; terminal throttling must not appear as an ongoing or successful retry.
- Scope that replacement to the message ID, not the entire user turn. A separate follow-up message must append to, never erase, a completed cost answer. Keep per-stream text state isolated and preserve errors, empty-message handling and replay consistency.
- Do not delay the primary answer for a follow-up tool call. Next actions are escaped `[label](prompt:instruction)` links in the answer; a last paragraph or list holding only such links renders as one row of buttons below it (`markdown.js`). There is no follow-up tool: `SuggestFollowUp` was removed because models called it in a round of its own (15-25 s each; once a turn ended with no answer). Old transcripts still replay their follow-up buttons.
- Replay redacted turn failures as explicit terminal notices, not assistant answers or vague reconnect pills. Live and restored errors share the same presentation, preserve partial results, and let the user edit the saved question without automatic resend or draft loss. Model inference authorization is separate from tenant sign-in.
- Render retry progress from server deadlines and eligibility, with a reactive clock and exact tool-call association. Do not show a frozen original wait, a hardcoded retry limit, HTTP 0 as throttling, or call-success/HTTP-failure as a green success.
- Escape all model/tool-influenced text before `v-html` transformations. Assistant Markdown goes through `src/markdown.js` (`renderMarkdown`), which escapes first, builds every element itself, allows only absolute http(s) links (new tab, `noopener noreferrer`) and never treats `_` inside a word or a spaced `*` as emphasis. A table column is numeric (right-aligned) only when its cells start with a figure or currency, so labels containing digits (`GPT-6 Astra`) stay text; headers wrap, figures and short code identifiers do not, and the first column stays pinned while a wide table scrolls.
- Only the explicit Stop action marks a response as stopped; an arbitrary `AbortError` is recoverable transport failure.
- A reloaded or busy-refused view of a running turn learns it from `/api/sessions/{id}/active` (`startedUtc`, `toolsCompleted`, `scheduled`). It shows elapsed time and finished tool calls and offers `.action-btn--stop`, which calls `/api/chat/stop`. Only a server-confirmed stop records the turn as stopped, and stale `/active` responses for another session are ignored.
- Attachment callbacks must update chips by stable `uid`, never by array index. Wait for uploads before sending, delist files whose chips were removed in flight, and revoke blob thumbnail URLs only after Vue unmounts them.
- Generated HTML previews must stay in a sandboxed iframe without `allow-same-origin`; model-produced deck scripts must never inherit access to application cookies, storage, DOM, or authenticated APIs.
- The social sharing card `public/og-image.png` (1200 × 630) is rendered from `src/Dashboard/frontend/social/og-image.html` with `npm run og-image`, using the app's font, colours and start-page questions. Re-render it when those change and bump the `?v=` query on `og:image` and `twitter:image` in `index.html` so platforms refetch it. README screenshots live in `docs/assets/readme/`; capture them from real answers (never tenant data) and keep them under about 600 KB each.

## Code conventions

- Follow Microsoft C# conventions and modern Vue Composition API patterns.
- Preserve public APIs unless the task requires a change.
- Keep API endpoints RESTful and ownership-checked.
- Use current stable Azure API versions. Document intentional older versions where a service has not adopted the newest family version.
- Prefer managed identity and OIDC over client secrets.
- Keep unrelated formatting out of functional changes.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` and this file whenever architecture, tools, security boundaries, dependencies, or project structure change.

## Local development

Secrets use .NET User Secrets; never commit local settings.

```powershell
cd src/Dashboard/frontend
npm ci
npm run build

cd ..
$env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = "Development"
dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5000
```

The frontend must be built before backend startup so `wwwroot` exists when ASP.NET resolves `WebRootPath`.

## Testing

- Backend: `dotnet build src/Dashboard/Dashboard.csproj --no-restore`
- Regressions: `dotnet test tests/Dashboard.Tests/Dashboard.Tests.csproj`; Python `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"`; frontend `npm run test` and `npm run test:browser`.
- `validate.yml` runs credential-free regressions, desktop/mobile browsers and Linux image smoke checks before either deployment workflow can run.
- Both deployment workflows also require `live-evaluations.yml`. Local and CI runs execute the same explicit set of 24 representative template/incident questions, four of them regressions from the session audit with a case-specific expectation appended to the rubric, against real inference and Azure tools; all 24 must pass. Keep the complete template catalog available for coverage, but never accept a subset, arbitrary replacement set or changed contracts. This is curated coverage, not a verified popularity ranking. Any failed, missing, timed-out, wrong-revision or invalid verdict blocks deployment. Use the dedicated evaluation identity/environment for CI and only explicitly authorized maintainer-lab identity/scopes locally, never production credentials or customer data. `EVAL_DATA_CLASSIFICATION=synthetic` publishes answers; `internal-test` (maintainer-owned test tenants) publishes only questions, tool outcomes, timings and pass/fail, withholding answers, error text and judge rationale from summaries and artifacts. When the optional repository variable `EVAL_DIAGNOSTICS_CERT` holds a maintainer's public RSA (≥3072-bit) certificate, a failed run also uploads `private-diagnostics.enc.json`: failed-case records encrypted with RSA-OAEP-256/AES-256-GCM, readable only with `tests/LiveEvaluations/Unprotect-Diagnostics.ps1` and the maintainer's non-exportable key. Never publish those records unencrypted, and never put a private key in the variable. The judge sees tool arguments, visible structured outputs, the host's connection context and the full session timeline (agent model/effort, total and first-token seconds, per-call start/end/duration/round and success, concurrency, tool versus model time, throttle notices, and budgets) alongside the answer, and grades end-to-end efficiency with its Azure API knowledge. See `tests/LiveEvaluations/README.md` for configuration and test-host versus delegated-browser coverage. Do not skip unavailable prerequisites or relax rubrics to make a run pass. The suite waits out reported service cooldowns between cases and re-runs a case once, unchanged, only when it failed after a final service throttle, and never earlier than one full Cost Management quota minute after the refusal; every other failure is final. Feature and production runs both use `EVAL_FAIL_FAST=true`, stopping at the first final case failure; the gate already requires every case, so the rest would only spend time and quota.
- Live gate runs require clean candidate application/evaluator/workflow sources, inherited build configuration, and matching evaluator/Dashboard assembly revisions. Replay must preserve the decoded question and every completed answer, not just echo the question. The evaluator shares the runtime's reported-tool-failure classifier; a positive judge cannot override failed execution. Private case captures stay outside published output, internal-test withholding applies locally too, and cancellation stops subsequent cases and cleans only owned process trees/captures. Environment-scoped evaluation secrets resolve on the job and remain mandatory at preflight. Manual `feature.yml` dispatch defaults to validation only (`deploy=false`); only an explicit `deploy=true` permits a manual test-slot deployment after both gates pass.
- Explicitly authorized local maintainer-lab evaluations may use the existing Azure CLI user session. Select its cached identity with the first approved evaluation subscription, verify that scope belongs to `EVAL_TENANT_ID`, and use that credential consistently for tools, candidate inference and the judge. Tenant-only CLI selection can target the wrong cached user, and CLI tenant/subscription options are mutually exclusive. Keep coordinates outside tracked files and never copy personal CLI tokens/cache into CI. GitHub evaluations still require their separate read-only OIDC identity; token issuance alone does not establish API access.
- Frontend: `npm run build` under `src/Dashboard/frontend`
- Local failed-evaluation diagnostics may be retained only with explicit `EVAL_PRIVATE_DIAGNOSTICS_DIRECTORY` outside the repository and published output (including symlink targets); CI rejects the option. Delete passing captures and never publish raw failed-tool details in either data classification.
- Preserve captured execution on credential, replay and judge exceptions. Private diagnostics include bounded redacted successful/failed tool details and failure phase, never reset completed work to an empty zero-duration record. Neither synthetic nor internal-test publication includes those private fields.
- Distinguish a valid negative judge verdict from malformed/missing judge output in gate diagnostics. Both fail the gate; acceptance requires the three boolean judge flags (`accepted`, `grounded`, `complete`) to be true, integer `avoidableCalls`/`avoidableRounds` and non-negative `avoidableSeconds` bounded by the session, a host-computed efficiency score of at least 3 on the 1-5 scale, and a nonempty reason, without publishing private rationale. The judge counts and names waste; `EvaluationGate.EfficiencyScore` maps counts to the rubric anchors so a model-chosen score cannot drift from them; a single avoidable call or round that added under a tenth of the elapsed time scores 4 (the user asked for a judge that is not too strict about negligible waste). Efficiency waste is clear waste (a third or uncorrected failed call, repeated, needlessly sequential, unfiltered-paging, unnecessary-lookup or unrelated calls). The agent is meant to research and self-correct: up to two failed calls each corrected by a later successful call to the same tool, one extra learning lookup, host-serialized Cost Management calls, throttle waits, exact result queries and configured reasoning time are not waste, and the deterministic gate allows up to two such corrected failures. The judge grades materiality, not polish (maintainer decision): an answer correct in substance that delivers every core requested result passes despite imperfect wording, depth or a missing optional caveat, while wrong or unsupported material claims (figures, prices, savings, resources, recommendations) and missing core results still fail. Fix a flagged inefficiency in the agent prompt or tool description, never by loosening the efficiency floor or time budgets. The judge's HTTP request alone resends unchanged after transient 408/429/5xx or transport failures (at most four attempts, `Retry-After` capped at 60 seconds); request, authorization and verdict failures are never retried.
- The judge checks every requested metric across all answer columns and visible outputs. Enabled prepaid inventory is not invoice-confirmed paid quantity, and assignments are not activity. Require all available counts and any supplied billing evidence, reject unsupported paid/waste claims, and keep missing required activity reports incomplete. The one maintainer-approved exception: a requested but unavailable report for a product with zero enabled and zero assigned seats makes the per-seat answers determinate (0 of 0, no licensed non-users, no inactive-seat waste) when the answer attributes them to zero seats and leaves unlicensed-user activity unknown. Do not change case rubrics to repair a judge's source-metric confusion.
- Always verify the rendered UI for UI changes; a successful build is not a browser test.
- Measure latency from the app's SSE stream, not rendered pixels.
- Before every send, wait for the composer to be enabled and for the Stop button to be absent.
- Select Stop only by `.action-btn--stop`.
- For authenticated UI runs, pin the exact tab the user shared and use `run_playwright_code` exclusively. Do not use high-level browser helpers or the separate `mcp_playwright_browser_*` surface. Never open or navigate a replacement tab; if shared access is lost, ask the user to re-share the same signed-in tab.
- Check console errors, page errors, failed requests, tool sequence/count, TTFT, total time, and persisted transcript.
- After edits, verify disk state with `git status --short`; save all editor buffers before building.

## Deployment

Pin every external GitHub Action to a full 40-character commit SHA with a release-version comment. Verify the SHA against the upstream release, and keep `cooldown.default-days: 7` in the `github-actions` Dependabot entry. Do not replace pins with mutable tags during workflow edits.

Customer deployment uses `azd up` and generates names from the selected environment. Never put deployment coordinates in tracked files.

Maintainer CI workflows read deployment settings from GitHub repository variables and secrets:

- Production variables: `PROD_ACR_NAME`, `PROD_ACR_LOGIN_SERVER`, `PROD_CONTAINER_IMAGE`, `PROD_WEBAPP_NAME`, `PROD_RESOURCE_GROUP`, `PROD_VERIFY_URL`
- Test variables: corresponding `TEST_*` names plus `TEST_SLOT_NAME`
- OIDC secrets: `AZURE_*` for test and `AZURE_PROD_*` for production

Feature deployments reuse the configured existing shared TEST slot, never create a slot per branch or swap production. Validate its exact Azure resource ID and actual hostname before writes; reject blank/production slots and mismatched verification URLs. Serialize settings/image writes without cancelling in-flight updates. Merge only the three evaluated model settings with `az webapp config appsettings set --slot`, preserving unrelated settings, and verify effective model settings plus full SHA/build/branch. Existing slot-configuration/registry permissions (no ARM deployment permission) and slot inference access are prerequisites, not grants the workflow may add. A slot has its own system-assigned identity. Provision it through `AZURE_PREVIEW_SLOT_NAME` (Standard or Premium plan) on the production web app and plan: `modules/preview.bicep` grants its identity AcrPull and Foundry User, and postprovision federates it. The slot must share the Foundry account's tenant; managed identities cannot be granted roles across tenants. `AZURE_PREVIEW_DEPLOY_SUBJECTS` adds the feature workflow's OIDC identity: Website Contributor on the slot only, Reader on the parent and AcrPush. Both Azure sign-in jobs use GitHub environment `test`, so one branch-independent subject serves every feature branch. Add a slot to an existing production site by deploying `modules/preview.bicep` alone; a full provision rewrites the CI-managed production image and model settings.

The protected evaluation endpoint comes from the `EVAL_MODEL_ENDPOINT` secret, never a plain variable. Successful evaluation exports the model, reasoning effort, full candidate SHA and normalized endpoint SHA-256 fingerprint. Feature deployment uses those values without model defaults and compares its endpoint secret locally before Azure login or writes; never expose raw endpoint coordinates or silently retarget inference.

Live evaluations use the evaluation identity, so they never prove the deployed identity. Both deployment workflows record the prior image and three model settings before writes. After the version check, `infra/scripts/deployment-smoke.mjs chat` must receive a completed anonymous answer through the deployed URL. On failure or cancellation after writes began, the workflow restores the recorded state and fails. Keep published smoke reasons redacted, and do not add `continue-on-error` or a skip path.

Production OIDC must be branch-scoped to `main` and least-privileged: `AcrPush` on the target registry and `Website Contributor` on the target web app. App Service pulls images with its own managed identity and `AcrPull`.

Do not deploy without explicit user instruction. When instructed, validate builds, diff, secrets, account context, workflow configuration, and target version before pushing.

## Observability

- Host traces use `SamplingRatio = 1` with `TracesPerSecond = null`; the rate limit otherwise overrides ratio sampling. Keep host and browser telemetry changes distinct. The host exports agent spans (`AzureFinOps.AI.Agent`, Agent Framework OpenTelemetry) directly to Azure Monitor; there is no collector sidecar.
- `ApiExceptionHandling` owns the correlated exception log for handled HTTP faults. Suppress the duplicate ASP.NET exception-handler diagnostic, retain the request metric's `error.type`, and keep framework diagnostics for faults after response start. Expected cancellation stays trace-only. Transcript ownership is rechecked under the user gate; a conflicting live owner fails closed without an exception-driven 500.
- Owner-bound turn outcomes persist for 30 days and reconcile interrupted records on startup. Normal chat fulfillment stays `not_evaluated`; a completed HTTP request or agent turn is not proof the user's objective was met.
- Record tool calls rejected before the protected callback, without double-counting acquired callbacks. A nonempty fallback answer after a failed tool is not clean execution; include failed non-evidence tools in partial outcome classification.
- Truly empty terminal turns emit a recoverable `empty_result` error. Explicit cancellation and structured chart/score/artifact outputs are not empty results; outcome fulfillment remains `not_evaluated`.
- Use the `investigate-ai-sessions` skill (`.github/skills/investigate-ai-sessions/SKILL.md`) for end-to-end completion audits: prove authorized owner-bound extraction first, sample distinct populated conversations rather than turns or warmups, and disclose full-event versus retained-message-only coverage. Keep historical customer transcripts and deployment coordinates out of source and regression fixtures.
- Browser exception capture has one bounded, redacted, deduplicated reporting path. Do not claim the historical notification-manager exception is fixed without reproducing its trigger.

Discover Application Insights and Log Analytics identifiers from `azd env get-values`, Azure Resource Graph, or the deployed resource group. Never hardcode an application ID, workspace ID, subscription, or resource group in prompts or instructions.

For workspace-based Application Insights, query the Log Analytics `AppExceptions`, `AppTraces`, `AppRequests`, and `AppDependencies` tables. Confirm telemetry pipeline activity before interpreting an empty exception result.
